position: Federal Reserve: Limit the Federal Reserve's lender-of-last-resort function; Minimum Effective Reforms
proposal: The chapter recommends limiting the Federal Reserve's lender-of-last-resort function, which it calls a standing bailout offer that encourages risky lending, with ample lead time so banks can adjust without disrupting the financial system (p. 733). Among its minimum effective reforms it recommends curbing the Fed's last-resort lending practices, which it ties to too big to fail and moral hazard (p. 740).

status_summary: No statutory or Board action limiting the Fed's lender-of-last-resort role or its last-resort lending was found. The activity found points the other way but is not a limit or an expansion of lending authority: S. 4585, the Discount Window Preparedness Act, introduced 2026-05-20 and referred to the Senate Banking Committee, would require larger banks to test-borrow from the discount window, direct the Board to modernize discount window operations and study ways to reduce stigma, and sets no cap on advances. In remarks of 2026-09-22 the Fed's Vice Chair reported that Reserve Banks had streamlined the Borrower-in-Custody collateral program in September 2026 and described primary credit as offered on a no-questions-asked basis; no limit on lending was announced.

timeline.event: S. 4585, the Discount Window Preparedness Act, was introduced and referred to the Senate Banking Committee; it would require discount window test borrowing by banks above 10 billion dollars in assets, direct the Board to modernize discount window operations, and require a stigma study, with no cap on advances.

The Fed's Vice Chair reported that Reserve Banks streamlined the Borrower-in-Custody collateral program in September 2026 to ease pledging of loans for discount window access; no limit on lending was announced.

title: Limit the Fed's lender-of-last-resort role and curb its last-resort lending
uncertainties: No 119th Congress bill amending section 13(3) or limiting discount window lending was found; congress.gov search could not be opened, so absence is not proven. The Fed's operational changes (the Borrower-in-Custody streamlining and the Discount Window Direct portal) make existing lending easier to reach but do not widen eligibility or lending authority, so the record is not staged diverged; a reader who treats easier access as opposite to the recommendation could stage it diverged. S. 4585 is an introduced bill and not operative, so it cannot set the stage. The Borrower-in-Custody change is known from the Vice Chair's remarks; the Fed web page announcing it was not opened. The American Banker article is context only.
